settings.label: About the house
settings.text: Ananta means without end. Vastram means cloth. The name is a description of the work: a length of handwoven cloth with no seam, woven on pit looms in Tamil Nadu, by weavers whose names we print on every piece.
settings.note: Ananta Vastram is a menswear house from Tamil Nadu. We make veshtis and the garments worn with them, in limited number; commissions are made to order. The people in our photographs are the wearers of the pieces, named with their consent.

settings.title: The loom decides first
settings.text:
A veshti is fixed before a thread is thrown: its width, its border, the kara at its edge. Kamalam Moorthy, who designs every piece, decides these first.

The cloth is silk cotton, with a weft spun by hand and woven on a pit loom. Borders carry zari. The embroidery is aari work in metallic thread, done by hand by our senior artisan.

A piece takes about six weeks from the loom to the last stitch. That time is the reason there are only a few of each.

settings.title: Every piece carries a name
settings.text: The weaver's name is woven into the label and printed on the page. It is not a credit. It is the record of who made the cloth, kept where the buyer can see it.

settings.title: Limited number
settings.text: Each design is made in a small, fixed number. When the last piece is placed, it is finished. It is not re-run.

settings.title: Commissions, made to order
settings.text: Everyday and Occasional pieces are woven ahead and ready to wear. A commission begins only when it is asked for, after a conversation, and you are told how long it will take.

settings.title: Worn by real people
settings.text: There are no models. Every photograph on this site is of someone who owns the piece, and we name them.

settings.title: One price
settings.text: The price is the price. There are no sales, no launch offers, and no marketplace listings.
